video_title: Bobby Marks Breaks Down Kings’ Surprising Nique Clifford Trade

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Kings' roster flexibility after waiving Nique Clifford
quotes.excerpt: they've got to sign a player within two weeks here. So we'll see what the direction there
quotes.quote: Now they've got two roster spots open. They've got to sign a player within two weeks here. So we'll see what the direction there. Certainly, I think you're probably looking at guard help as far as with that. And it gives you some flexibility, financial flexibility, and as you pick up a couple future seconds in 2028 and 2030 and everything like that. So I think there's probably a short-term play and certainly a long-term play.
quotes.social_post: The Kings now have two open roster spots after waiving Nique Clifford. Bobby Marks expects the team to prioritize adding guard help in the next two weeks.

quotes.speaker: Allen Stiles
quotes.summary_phrase: Kings' trade acquisition of Nique Clifford from the Spurs
quotes.excerpt: that was the 2027 first from the Spurs and that was straight up the Kings' pick

text_blocks.speaker: Allen Stiles
text_blocks.text: We were double checking how the Kings acquired Nique Clifford. That was the 2027 first from the Spurs and that was straight up the Kings' pick, right? And then they added those protections to give it to OKC. And it probably is going to go to OKC. That's a pretty big commitment for one Nique, isn't it, Bobby?

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: It was actually the Spurs' first. It was the San Antonio first that you got. They traded it, they got in the Fox deal and then they traded it originally. They traded it to Oklahoma City to get the draft rights of Nique in the draft in 2025. So yeah, the optics aren't great when you look at basically Oklahoma City gets the player, they the draft rights of the player they traded, but now in a trade a year later, and also have that Spurs pick because it will likely fall between 17 and 30.

quotes.social_post: The optics are not great for the Kings. Oklahoma City essentially gets the player they traded away a year ago back, plus the Spurs first round pick.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Risk of trading players Sam Presti wants
quotes.excerpt: if Sam Presti wants a guy, then I don't want to I don't want to maybe you shouldn't get rid of him
quotes.quote: I think you're where Oklahoma City is and where Sacramento is. I think they're in two different levels here as far as for where they're building the roster and everything. It blew up in Philadelphia's face last year when they traded Jared McCain to the Thunder and I know they picked up a first-round pick that turned into LeBaron Philon here. But yeah, I mean I think if you, you know, listen, if Sam Presti wants a guy, then I don't want to I don't want to maybe you shouldn't get rid of him. There's nothing like it. So definitely.
quotes.social_post: Bobby Marks on dealing with Sam Presti: If the Thunder GM wants a guy, maybe you should not get rid of him. It blew up in Philadelphia's face last year.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Challenges of trading Zach LaVine's contract
quotes.excerpt: when you're trading a $49 million contract, there is some challenges, certainly, as you guys know with these rules
quotes.quote: I just think Zach's number is so big. You know, I think certainly when you're trading a $49 million contract, there is some challenges, certainly, as you guys know with these rules, the inability to take back more money. I think he would be more of a guy that, you know, Kings fans don't want to hear this, that he would be more of a buyout guy when you get to February here. But I think, of course, you want to, you know, you're not going to trade him to the Knicks and you're not going to trade him to the Warriors.
quotes.social_post: Bobby Marks on a potential Zach LaVine trade: Kings fans might not want to hear this, but he would be more of a buyout guy when you get to February.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Kings' salary cap outlook and long-term commitments
quotes.excerpt: really the only long-term commitment, big money-wise is Keegan, that stretches out a bunch of years
quotes.quote: It's clean. When you look at kind of where the money they've got committed to, Zach's number will come off the books this year. DeAndre's number, he's on an expiring $25 million contract. Really the only long-term commitment, big money-wise is Keegan, that stretches out a bunch of years here. And then you've got a bunch of guys making between $2 million to $8 million here. So yeah, they're in really good shape. I think they have to figure out does it make sense to prioritize they've got potential to have cap space this summer.
quotes.social_post: The Kings are in good shape financially. With Zach LaVine's number coming off the books and DeAndre's expiring contract, the only big long-term money is Keegan Murray.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Uncertainty of NBA lottery reform for teams
quotes.excerpt: I think the lottery reform is an unknown. I mean if you've you would wake up this morning
quotes.quote: I think the lottery reform is an unknown. I mean if you've you would wake up this morning and be like, wow, Sacramento's got a really good chance of getting the number one pick. And you're and then you say, no, you don't want to be picking you don't want to go into the lottery with you know, being in the top three just based on relegation as far as the ability to probably more likely to pick in the 8, 9, 10 range here. So yeah, there is an unknown there because there's not an incentive there's not an incentive to lose, which we would have seen in the past.
quotes.social_post: Bobby Marks on lottery reform: There is an unknown there because there is not an incentive to lose, which we would have seen in the past.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Salary cap circumvention investigations for Bucks and Clippers
quotes.excerpt: Milwaukee is really in there because of the Gary Trent situation where they're being investigated for salary cap circumvention
quotes.quote: There's a couple teams in there. OKC, New York and we actually put Milwaukee in there. And Milwaukee is really in there because of the Gary Trent situation where they're being investigated for salary cap circumvention. And if there's a ruling on that, that they've violated the cap, they're going to get penalties similar to the Clippers, but they're going to be significant. And that's certainly not what you want when you're a rebuilding team post-Shai. I think with OKC, based on where their payroll is going to be next year with Shai's supermax hitting, fortunately for them they've got 13, 14 guys under contract and they have three first-round picks upcoming. They have the ability to swap first with the Clippers here. They're still in somewhat of a good situation, but their payroll is going to get significantly higher. And of course, New York, you're going to have to figure out the town situation, who's eligible for an extension, the same with Josh Hart.
quotes.social_post: Milwaukee is being investigated for salary cap circumvention regarding the Gary Trent situation. If they are found to have violated the cap, they will face significant penalties.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Darius Ainge's development and learning curve
quotes.excerpt: I think this is going to be a big learning curve for him, playing 82 games
quotes.quote: I love him. I thought, listen, this is going to be a big learning curve for him, playing 82 games and the travel component, the losing component, a lot of that here. But I think for him, it's just kind of getting better each day. It's he's seeing a lot of different he's seeing all these it's like going through the batting order for the first time, all these different teams that he's seeing here. But I think he's a fearless player. I think he will make his teammates better. I know his attempts are a little bit high, probably not where you want them, but I think he's certainly aggressive and I think the one thing you don't want him is to lose the confidence that he has right now.
quotes.social_post: On Darius Ainge: It is a big learning curve with the travel and losing, but he is a fearless player who will make his teammates better.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.excerpt: We haven't seen a November trade since James Harden in 2024
quotes.quote: We haven't seen a November trade since James Harden in 2024 and that was certainly a different circumstance because Harden had asked out. So yeah, it's it's usually I always say like you probably have a good idea identity about your team like 20 games in. And then when we get to December 15th, because that's when most restrictions are lifted for guys who sign free agent contracts, gives teams more flexibility, you see a little bit more movement. But yeah, November trades are a rare commodity.
quotes.social_post: November trades are a rare commodity in the NBA. Teams usually wait until December 15th when most free agent signing restrictions are lifted to gain more flexibility.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Reasons for early-season trades and roster adjustments
quotes.excerpt: they got a bunch of injuries, they need a guy right now, they're running out of bodies
quotes.quote: Every trade is done, you know, like in Oklahoma City, like, hey, there's they got a bunch of injuries, they need a guy right now, they're running out of bodies. They want to preserve some of these players. They're going to be a little more aggressive in November than maybe some other teams are. I think with a guy like DeAndre, it's basically, you know, you got an expiring contract. Where are we? Do we need depth on our wings as you got it, we want to resign. I think those probably take a little bit longer. That's probably when you get into like, you know, January, unless there's a pressing need.
quotes.social_post: Teams are more aggressive in November if they have a pressing need due to injuries. Otherwise, roster moves for expiring contracts usually take until January.
